guard: Every credential that runs the endpoint-stream creation seam holds a STREAM.UPDATE row for each store that seam hardens right after creation, and for no other stream. Core names those stores once; the provisioner and the restore-side infrastructure login both read that list.
why: The admission and issued stores joined the hardening step with their provisioner grant, and the restore
login kept its hand-written records-only update row. A live `up --restore` then stopped at the
listener-bind boundary: Permissions Violation for Publish to $JS.API.STREAM.UPDATE.KV_cotal_issued_<s>.
Neither side's own unit could see it. The list is now one core export and this suite pins the login to
it; the mutation drops one hardened store from the list so the login is minted without its row.

mutations.name: the admission store leaves the hardened list (the restore login is minted without its update row)
mutations.expectRed: the hardened list names the records, issued, accepted and admission stores
mutations.cell: the hardened list names the records, issued, accepted and admission stores
